## What was wrong

Three places in the rotor pipeline treated the *written direction* of a reaction as physically meaningful, so relabeling atoms or applying `ts.reverse` changed the rotor coordinates of the very same transition state:

1. **`ts_linear_reacting_atom_keys`** (`_03kekule.py`) detected sigma radicals only in the **reactants** graph. A sigma-radical center is linear whether it shows up among reactants or products, so it silently vanished when the reaction was written backwards.
2. **`linear_segment_cap_keys`** (`_03kekule.py`) extended a linear segment to its collinear "cap" atoms via `atom_neighbor_atom_key`'s default `ords_last=(0.1,)`, i.e. it deprioritized *forming* bonds only. Reversing swaps 0.1↔0.9, so a different atom got picked as in-line — this was the direct cause of the fixture's disagreement (`(79,67,37,53)` forward vs `(23,11,67,79)` reverse).
3. **`rotational_coordinates`** (`_06heur.py`) chose dihedral reference atoms with the same forming-only rule, an independent copy of the same asymmetry.

## The fix

- `_00core.py`: named the TS bond-order convention (`TS_FORMING_BOND_ORDER`, `TS_BREAKING_BOND_ORDER`, `TS_REACTING_BOND_ORDERS`) and used it at every definitional site; taught `atom_sorted_neighbor_atom_keys` (and the wrappers up to `atom_zmat_neighbor_atom_key`) to accept **groups** of bond orders that rank as equivalent, so forming and breaking can be de-prioritized *alike* rather than one before the other.
- `_03kekule.py`: new public `in_line_neighbor_atom_keys`, which identifies collinear neighbors from physics — sp-hybridized centers in whichever reagent structure they are sp, plus atoms across reacting bonds of reacting atoms that become linear — instead of an arbitrary symbol sort; sigma radicals now taken from both reagent graphs; dummy atoms excluded since they are perpendicular by construction.
- `_06heur.py`: reference-atom selection now treats reacting bonds as one equivalence class.
